ideas: No commuting means more time and energy

phrases.meaning: the group of skilled people available

model: I think employees should be allowed to work fully remotely, as long as they can do their jobs well. First, remote work cuts out the commute, which saves a huge amount of time and energy. For example, before the pandemic, I spent almost two hours a day in Hanoi traffic. Since my company introduced a flexible schedule, I've been using that time to exercise and cook proper meals, and I've actually stayed more productive. Another reason is that companies can hire from a much bigger talent pool. My team has recently hired a designer who lives in Da Lat, and she's been doing brilliant work without ever visiting the office. Of course, some people feel isolated without face-to-face interaction, so managers should decide on a case-by-case basis and perhaps organise regular meetups. But overall, if people can strike a balance that works for them, I believe fully remote work should be an option.
